text:
alex: hey team — first day epics: running our repo's docker-compose on my M1 mac, Postgres container dies during init. Error: "initdb: could not change permissions of directory "/var/lib/postgresql/data": Permission denied". I'm using a bind mount to ./pgdata. any quick fixes?

maya: welcome! :wave: common culprit is the host bind mount ownership/permissions on mac. two quick paths: use a named docker volume instead of a host bind, or chown the host dir to the postgres UID.

sam: +1. On official Postgres images the db user often runs as UID 999. Try: `sudo chown -R 999:999 ./pgdata` and `chmod 700 ./pgdata` then `docker-compose up`.

alex: tried chown but still failing — maybe Docker Desktop on mac has some weird mapping. any docker-desktop specific tips?

maya: yes — Docker Desktop for Mac (especially newer gRPC FUSE / virtiofs) can behave oddly. I usually avoid host bind mounts for PG data on mac. Use a named volume in compose:

``` 
services:
  db:
    image: postgres:15
    volumes:
      - pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data

volumes:
  pgdata:
```

Then `docker-compose up` will use a managed volume which avoids host FS permission issues.

sam: if you need the files on host (for dumps/dev reasons) you can still create the volume and then copy out a dump. Or pre-create the host dir and set the correct owner inside a temporary container: `docker run --rm -v $(pwd)/pgdata:/data alpine chown -R 999:999 /data` — that maps through docker and runs chown as root inside container so it affects the mounted dir.

alex: nice. Is there any gotcha with Apple Silicon images? I saw some posts about arm64 vs amd64 and init scripts failing.

maya: good call — prefer the arm64 postgres images (they're multi-arch as `postgres:15`), but if your compose pins `platform: linux/amd64` it will emulate and might complicate UID things. If nothing else works, try `image: postgres:15` without forcing platform.

infra-bot: reminder: for local dev we recommend named volumes + PGDATA env var set to `/var/lib/postgresql/data/pgdata` in the compose file to avoid permission-intolerant init. See onboarding doc: https://intranet.redwood.dev/dev-setup#db

sam: one more: if initdb insists on 700 perms, `sudo chmod 700 ./pgdata` on host helps. Also make sure the directory isn't owned by root on mac in a way that Docker can't override (Docker Desktop file sharing settings).

alex: okay will try switching to named volume + chown via alpine trick. thanks y'all, saved my afternoon :relieved:

maya: ping if it still fails — we can jump on a quick call and pair through docker settings.

alex: will do, thanks!
